name: East Greenland Current
scope: Regional outer/slope EGC reference corridor from the Fram Strait section at 78.5 degrees N to the study’s southern shelf boundary at 59 degrees N in the Cape Farewell region. Excludes a distinct East Greenland Coastal Current axis, interior export branches, upstream Arctic extensions and onward West Greenland Current. The 59 degrees N gate is the paper’s regional boundary, not a precise geographic coordinate of Cape Farewell.
layer: Outer/slope EGC geographic corridor only; no velocity layer, bathymetric axis or transport diagnosed. Separate from the near-surface coastal current.
time_convention: General editorial reference corridor. The source analyzes VIKING20X and GLORYS12 during 1993–2019; this sketch is not their time-mean or instantaneous model axis.
source_locator: Introduction: distinctions among EGCC, shelfbreak branch and outer/slope EGC, and Fram Strait–Cape Farewell focus. Section 2.1.1: East Greenland shelf from the 78.5 degrees N section to the 59 degrees N study boundary; Figure 1 caption identifies a 1000 m offshore shelf boundary.
source_citation: Schiller-Weiss, I., Martin, T., Karstensen, J., and Biastoch, A. (2023), Do Salinity Variations Along the East Greenland Shelf Show Imprints of Increasing Meltwater Runoff?, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans 128, e2023JC019890.
source_license: CC BY-NC article; factual geographic reference only. No source figure, contour, velocity field or provider geometry copied into this candidate.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects coarse offshore regional waypoints and longitudes to sketch the southward east Greenland corridor. Source latitude boundaries and regional/branch description constrain the sketch; these vertices are not published model coordinates, a digitized figure path or observed current-axis positions. Source study shelf/1000 m definitions do not establish these vertices as a diagnosed isobath. An initial broad offshore sketch was revised toward the east Greenland margin; a trial 43 degrees W vertex at 61 degrees N intersected the coarse atlas land mask and was rejected.
scenario_rule: Three uniform longitude shifts (-0.25/0/+0.25 degrees) crossed with independent start/end latitude shifts (-0.5/0/+0.5 degrees): 27 editorial scenarios. Not a source-reported error interval and does not exhaust branch choices or meanders.
remaining_gates: Check the coarse offshore vertices against source-defined outer/slope branch geography and a reproducible bathymetric corridor.
Independent review of the 78.5–59 degrees N regional convention and branch transitions, including convergence with the Irminger Current south of 64 degrees N.
Canonical claim, geometry and measurement integration; retain regional scope and keep coastal current separate.
